interactions.title: Kaeso arrives and talks with Wazir
lines: DM: ((Further political background)) Kaeso, a scholar from Chardon with several mutual friends with Wazir, arrives at the start of October. ((Further political background)) Kaeso and Wazir could frequently be found in long evening chats as the days grew shorter, wondering what these events meant for Mawar. Could it be long before Chardon looked to claim Mawar itself? ((Further political background))

before: DM: But in… in… the Mawar Confederacy in Hamri, the winter is bitterly cold and storm-lashed, with repeated gales and then hard freezes that leave ice lingering far longer than it should. The town hunkers down. It's a winter of hunger and hardship, where people speak in low voices of nightmares and strange songs on the wind, though no supernatural danger ever really emerges. But the ordinary dangers are enough: cold, hunger, and isolation take the toll, and for many families, that's a winter of loss. Little news comes in or out, and the Leviathan stands quiet through the long, hard winter.

DM: Into April, when spring comes late: a month of dreary rain and shuttered harbors, weeks of gray weather, half-drowned roads… mud. It's not till May of that year that the winter… that the weather finally breaks. And as spring turns to summer, the port of Hamri fills with news and trade.

DM: Wild rumors from the north of an ancient black dragon, a vicious beast that defeated even the best Chardonian legions, and drove the orc warlord Grumella before him in fear, finally killed by the heroes of the Battle of Voltara. From Chardon, the tales in the spring repeat the common refrains. The merchants and traders tell stories of the wealth and glory of empire. Others tell stories of the tightening fists of the wizards of the Academy. Rumors of scholarly expeditions sent to plunder treasure, ancient artifacts of magic and power from all points of the compass. But none of these expeditions ever come to Mawar, or at least not to Hamri, and it's hard to tell if these are just stories.

DM: The summer is cool and glorious, the hunting good. Ryu has many fine catches of large tuna. The Leviathan is full of the usual make-believe stories from far away, demons and centaurs fighting in the deserts of Dunmar. Inland lizardfolk villages vanishing without a trace, a haunted ghost of a dragon raiding on the shores of Lake Philandras. Who can really say what is true and what's just a… a pretty song told for coin?

DM: As summer turns to fall, rumors spread from the south of a daring theft, the merchants say. Powerful magic stolen from a great wizard of Chardon, who was viciously attacked and betrayed by outsiders in the city. Something about a giant's crown full of ancient elemental magic. A particularly daring captain of a Chardonian ship spent an evening trying to harass the guests of the Leviathan with description of these thieves. A halfling, an elf, a human, and a dwarf—but was quickly tossed out by Wazir.
after: DM: By the first storm of winter, more news. There was a war against orcs somewhere off far to the east, spreading through Dunmar and tearing the land apart. Kaeso took this hard and spent many days alone in his room, but emerged to say that Dunmar held, though he would not say how he knew. That winter was mild, but still little traffic came to Hamri. The news is always slow during the cold months, when the winter gales prevent ships from traveling.

DM: Spring arrived—of 1749—with news of peace, it seems the fighting in Dunmar was over, though tales differed about who was king now there. But few in Hamri really cared about the events of far-off Dunmar. The traders from Chardon whispered that something seemed wrong. While the amount of chalyte flowing into the city was greater than ever, constant shortages led to the first outbreak of cholera in years, though Kaeso would point out, the traders don't seem to count the sickness that spreads in the slums of the North Bank there. It was getting harder to ignore the growing number of people wandering the city, their minds consumed by chalyte overuse.

DM: It is now May 26, 1749. Not long ago, news reached Hamri of a vicious, unprovoked magical attack at the heart of Chardon itself, caused by none other than two of the thieves, Kenzo, a Dunmari spy, and Delwath, an evil elf, corrupted by shadows. Many had died in the Colorless Market as a fragment of Pandemonium was ripped into this world. Fausto, one of the leaders of the wizards, was pressing for war, and it seemed the Magistrates would comply. Some rumors claim that Fausto was already marching at the head of a column of war wizards, claiming he alone, rightly, could command the ancient wizardly might of Chardon. But these far-off events so far have not touched Mawar or Hamri particularly, beyond the news that spread through the tables and firesides of the Leviathan Inn.

DM: And as we pick up… in… in the evening of a pleasantly warm spring day, Wazir has asked Ryu, Trok, Nerissa, and Ander to join him to hear the strange tale of a woman just arrived. But first… If anybody has any comments about what their characters have been doing for the past 18 months, we will look back upon… the past. Time skip. But nobody's obligated.
Ryu: First off, that was awesome. Yeah. Amazing.

interactions.title: Rayna’s story and plea
lines: DM: This woman, Rayna, begins to tell you her story, and she's come looking for somebody. ((Discussion of Wazir helping strangers))

DM: She's in her, you know, mid-30s and brown skin. Clearly spends a lot of time at sea, like, weathered, like, salt-blown hair tied up, she's wearing, you know, practical sailor's outfit, but, like, every… you know, clearly this… this woman is a sailor through and through, right? She's, you know, everything about her demeanor and her dress suggests that she spends a lot of time at the ocean. I almost said Welby would recognize a kindred spirit, but Welby's not here. She has, piercing green eyes, sort of salt-blown… brown, black, sort of muddled hair that's curly and sort of tied back, wearing a white linen shirt, leather vest, sturdy breeches.

DM: And she looks up over at Wazir and looks at all of you and begins speaking in sort of a low voice. Initially directing at Wazir and saying, you know, she hopes she's been… everything she's been told, you're… you're a person who can be trusted. And… she has nowhere else to turn to, so… she hopes… Ta-da you know, what she's heard is true, and…

DM: She says she's come to town because she's having dreams, or more precisely, hearing voices in the waves. This is not new, she says. She was born… at sea. She never knew her father, and her mother was kind of too busy to pay much attention to her, but she was raised by her maternal grandfather, Caleb, who would tell her all these stories about Mawar. I mean, she is… she was Mawarin by descent, even though she doesn't live… probably not from Hamri, from somewhere else in Mawar. I'm… Her grandfather, Caleb, would tell her all these stories of the golden age of Mawar, proud heritage, all of this. And so, in her tea… and she would hear stories of the Ocean Watchers, too, and of the, sort of… strange tales, they said. Hold on one sec… You know, these strange tales of how the ocean… ocean behaved.

DM: And so, in her teens, when the ocean started to talk to her, she says she was not as, maybe, surprised as most others would be. She could never understand the words, but somehow they painted pictures of strange undersea cities of kelp forests full of memories, but also of Mawar long ago, of Guzo the Mariner standing on the prow of a ship. Guzo the Mariner is, like, one of the… heroes of Mawar, it's like… it's like a local… he's like a local saint, basically. People… send their prayers to the Eight Divines via Guzo, at least in Hamri. And there's a bunch of these other, like, heroes of Mawar that function as saints. She was fascinated, and her father said she was… her grandfather said she was blessed.

DM: Ten years ago, she says… The songs of the ocean suddenly stopped. She awoke from a nightmare of ripping and tearing to silence for the first time in years. Caleb was nervous, not sure what it meant. But for a while, they didn't think much of it. A few years after that, the ship was wrecked, and most of the crew, including Caleb, died, Rayna survived, but it was a dark few years after that recovering.

DM: But that's not why she's here, she says. She's here because a couple of weeks ago, the song suddenly returned. Ocean started speaking to her again. It's saying… About something trapped under a rock, but resting on waves. It felt scared, nervous, but it wanted this… fragment of song, fragment of its voice back.

DM: She saw cliffs with towers perched like teeth and a statue of Guzo the Mariner on a white sandy beach. Warm glow… warm glowing blue light filling the space, some kind of cave, maybe? The cliffs in her image look like Hamri, and… Guzo was always associated with Hamri in Caleb's stories, and so she came here. She doesn't know where it is, but she thinks somewhere in the cliffs of… of Hamri. There must be… cave with a white sandy beach and a statue of Guzo. And somewhere inside the cave is something that this song of the ocean wants back. And she would like somebody to find this. And bring it to her. And she… just hopes that you will help.

interactions.title: The stranded spokesman accepts Trok’s authority
lines: DM: So, you hear a cry that’s like “Hey, there’s people here,” and then another one shouts to you, like, “What are you doing here?” “Are you here to rescue? Are you here to rescue us? Ha ha ha ha ha ha.” Another one says, “They don’t look like they’re rescuers,” and starts to sort of inflate a little bit and draw up to his full form.
Ander: “We come in peace,” shouts Ander. Pulling out a sword as large as himself.
DM: Can you say that in Primordial?
DM: So, you yell in Primordial, “Hey, do you need rescuing?” And one of them… one of them yells out, to the others: “Hey! One of them speaks!”
DM: And the other says, to you, to Ryu: “Yeah, actually, we’ve been trapped here for, like, a week.”
Wazir: Is there anything obvious that's keeping them from getting into the water?
Nerissa: Should we ask them where they want to go?
Trok: Say, what's… what's keeping you here?
DM: In Primordial. “Boss man says we can’t leave without some crystal thing. Bossman went looking for it and hasn’t come back.”
Nerissa: Maybe we're here to rescue Bossman.
Trok: Tell us about boss man.
DM: Oh, he doesn't like asking questions. Came here straight away. Sad. You know, we’ll bring it back. Get big favor. Be heroes. Very nice.
Trok: ((Intimidation setup)) “Listen. I'm the new boss man. You're gonna help us. We're gonna find the crystal thing.”

DM: So, the one who's speaking to you, like, looks a little bit… shaken, and… they seem to… they seem to… to quaver a bit, and… questioning, “Are you really? I mean, you can speak. But can you bring us home?”
Trok: Oh yeah, of course! Listen. Bossman's boss sent us. Don't worry about the details. He'll just go up on it ahead of us. Gaza!

DM: Some, somebody, somebody yells out, hey. This… this one who speaks, yells out, says they work for Gazankoa. And you can see two more, kind of, come out from the sides here. Who look a little bit bigger and… and bossier, and then another one. Man… Really?
DM: So maybe somebody is here to rescue us.
Trok: Not exactly. We're just finishing the job, or I should say you are.
DM: Go ahead. The boss man went into the temple and never came back.
DM: Boss man could kill all of us. If he didn't come back, we're definitely not coming back.
Ryu: Well, why don't we go in and check it out? You all stay out here, we'll go in and check it out.
Trok: I look back, I guess we're doing good cop, bad cop, huh?

Trok: Strolls over to the stairs and picks up the largest piece of door fragment and says… “Look. We got a job to do. It's pretty clear who's in charge here, isn't it? Now… I’m given the orders. You go ahead… Or… You know what's gonna happen.” And he lifts the… door piece, threatening.

DM: ((Check bookkeeping)) They kind of shake a little bit. And they, they look up, “Okay, okay, we'll go with you.” Right. And the two, like, bigger ones, who are sort of leaders are, like, “We’re gonna stand watch,” and… and this… this one… And this…
Trok: Oh, I see. You're the brave ones, huh?
DM: This one… come with you, as you walk into the temple. ((Map controls))

before: Trok: Oh, I do.
DM: Ryu and Trok do, maybe?
Trok: Well, hi.
DM: That's… so instead of… from your subclass, you would normally get giant, but I think Primordial makes more sense for the tattoo artist.
Trok: Hmm.
after: DM: So… The entry room here is… again, mostly full of just debris. If battle does break out, this would all be difficult terrain, but there's also plenty of not only pieces of wood for Trok, but also, it's like there was… there's windows that were sort of broken, so there's, like, pieces of, like, metal spikes, and also pieces of glass.
Trok: Oh, yeah.
DM: And as you step forward, is anybody else going with Trok, or is it just Trok?
Ander: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
Wazir: Yeah, yeah.

review.reason: The negotiation has several anonymous voices; only the explicit spokesman is focal and no individual combat identity is inferred.

interactions.title: Trok tests the glowing altar
lines: Trok: So Trok is casually dangling a giant shard of glass from one hand and holding a metal spike in the other, and he says, “You.” He waves one forward. “Go up to that altar.”
DM: Sort of creep slowly towards the altar. “There’s nothing here, I promise!”
Trok: Isn't there, like, isn't there some kind of glowing crystal inside there? That's the source of the blue light.

DM: It's not a… it's not a crystal, it's just the altar itself is glowing with this blue light, and it sort of drift, like, a mist that flows down off of the altar. I guess in the picture, it looks a little like a crystal, but… It's not.

DM: Kind of slowly, like, looks back and, and… this… this one, this other one is, like, hanging back, and this guy, like, looks back, but the, like, bigger leaders are nowhere to be seen, and just kind of… steps forward. Okay… “Nothing’s happening.”
Trok: Good job. You won’t be receiving a glass shard bonus.

before: DM: So over here, there's a door that leads into… like, you could see this on the outside, there's, like, a… building on the side that has stained glass, and then there once were stairs, that went up, and there was a second floor over on this side, but that's gone. There are stairs. But who did we lose? There are stairs over here that lead down. What else do you see? And…
Trok: Wait, where is the… where are the stairs going down?
DM: On the top… they're not on the map, but on the top left. Over here.

DM: And then… Sorry, let me just double check. There's… there's a bunch of, like, sort of decorations around the edges, right? So towards the back, you can see that there's a bunch of these… or I guess it's more along the side walls, like here and here, sort of in between these columns. There's a bunch of, like, niches and things where little offerings and things have been scattered. You can see that many of them have been sort of strewn around the floor.

DM: In the back, it's like one of those medieval churches where there's, like, a whole bunch of… carvings in the wall, like, people's names and things, and then written in big letters up across the top in a sort of arc are the words in Mawarin: “Kneel and pray Guzo’s ancestor’s prayer to open the passage to the sea.” And then there's a door over here that leads into a side chapel. And the… No. Water creatures are just kind of standing, they, like, move forward, but they don't want to seem to want to get too close to the altar, and they're just kind of standing around a little bit, like… Like, he told us to wait on the beach and went in here and never came out.
after: Trok: Trok goes over to investigate, the offerings.
DM: Okay. Anybody else doing anything?
Ryu: Yeah, I'll search around.
Ander: I'll take a look over in the side room.
DM: Okay?

interactions.title: Three books recovered from the chapel
lines: DM: Meanwhile, Ander and Nerissa, searching around the chapel. Again, not like most of the contents of this room have been have been ruined. But there is a small, stone chest that you find buried under some debris. Not locked, but watertight enough that what's in it, which is a… three books, one, like, a book of… like, a book of common prayer, like a book with all the, like, prayers, various ancestor prayers to the different saints, things like that. One, a nicely illustrated, like… what is illuminated, like, with the fancy decorated letters and things.

DM: Just tale of stories. They seem to be, like, miracles of Mos Numena, but all in the context of these, like, local saints, right? It's, like, the stories of the saints. And the other… seems to be… I don't know if a ledger is the right word, but it's like a… or a guest book, it's like, people would write prayers to their… or have the priest write if they weren't literate, or have somebody write, like, the caretaker of this shrine, like… you know, so-and-so came and… it's like the guestbook for the temple, but it's like prayers for the… for whoever. There's a bunch of pages ripped out of this. It seems like people would write in them, and then after some time, they'd, like, rip out the pages and, I don't know, offer it to the statue. You don't know what would have happened, but it's like a book of… of people's hopes and dreams. And all of them are significantly damaged, but still readable in many places.

before: DM: You don't see anything, obviously, out of the ordinary in the, in the… temple area. But, well, Ander and… and, Nerissa are searching the, the sort of chapel. As you're kind of coming up blank, Wazir is, like, holding up his wand and it… pulses immediately towards the back. Where's my pointer? Towards, like, this back wall right here.
Wazir: I'll go in for a secret door in the back wall.
Trok: Alright.
Wazir: It's bossing.

DM: With the wand pointing you in that direction, you can see that there's water, sort of slight bit of water, like, oozing underneath the wall here, clearly a seam, and that there's a slight crack. But… No obvious means to open it.
after: DM: So, you returned… all now to the main room, where… yes! Guy has crept out. And this one says, “Okay, now what are you doing?” to Trok. “You seem to be just looking around.”
Trok: That's… that's correct. We're looking for something. What are we looking for again? The crystal. Yes, sir.
DM: Slowly… He steps back.
Ryu: Should I go get Rayna, and, like, escort her in here?
Trok: Isn't she, like, sailing the ship for us?

interactions.title: The prayer book opens the hidden chamber
lines: Nerissa: Nerissa flips through the prayer book to see if there's one called Guzo's Ancestor Prayer.
DM: ((Door investigation)) But Nerissa does, in fact, find, in the prayer book, the…
((Investigating and proposing other ways to open the door))

Nerissa: Nerissa reckons maybe the acoustics are better if she kneels down, so she kneels down and, directs towards the door a sort of sing-song chant of the prayer that she's reading, informed by the vibe of the… the insight she's gained from flipping through some stories of the devout. We've come to this place.
DM: As you begin to sing song this prayer, you can see… As you finish the words of the prayer, the door… just, like, vanishes. ((Map interface discussion))

before: Trok: Mmm.
Wazir: And there's a, clearly, ocean behind this secret door, right? There's one.
DM: Water coming out, yes. Right.
Wazir: Does it seem like it opens in or out, or is it just, like, totally impossible to tell?

DM: It's probably magic. Like, there's no hinges. There's no way to see that there's… It's not like a secret door that's secret, because it's, like, carefully hidden from… it's not some… well, at least not… well, go ahead and make an investigation check.
after: Trok: Nicer, yeah.
Ryu: Whoa, what is that behind the door?

DM: Behind… so in the… Oh… oh boy. So, the… this secret door opens a… it slides open, and you can see that there's a chamber, behind it. The blue light is more intense in here. And standing, like, holding this crystal, but seemingly, like, unable to move is… large… watery creature with a, like… water elemental, like… their body kind of turns into waves towards the ground. But then, as… forms into arms and a torso covered in, sort of, scales and spines. But as they turn and stare at you. It almost seems, as if their body itself is, like, all made of water, and they're just manifesting this shape on top of the water. They nearly entirely fill this space, but they seem… and again, like I said, the blue light is more intense in here, you can see the crystal. And it's not obvious that this… this creature doesn't move towards you, initially.
Nerissa: Are Trok's friends still here? Any of them?

DM: One of Trok's friends is still here, and yells, “Bossman! They’re here to help! From Gazankoa! They’re gonna bring the crystal to him!” And the creature turns and looks at you. And says in this rumbling voice, “Is that so?”

Wazir: Wait, wait, wait, wait, I'll cast Enlarge Reduce and enlarge you. Was it, was.
((Intimidation checks, growth description and table discussion))
DM: The creature, like, genuinely… shudders slightly and looks up at you as you grow. Like, you have… very unusual companions. But, I…

DM: If we… “If we can get out of this damn blue light, I can take you back to the plane of water. I will even let you present the crystal to Gazankoa.” And… she turns and gives you the crystal. Problems. “Let us go.”
Wazir: Is the blue light something obvious here? Like, can we all see a blue light? Like, is this just a little blue… like, is it filling the room?

DM: The entire… sorry, I described this a few times, but maybe you missed it. I shouted for days for them to open this damn door, and they just ignored me.”
DM: So… your rescue is welcome.
DM: Gazankoa's favor will fall heavily on you.
Trok: We'll give Gazankoa the full story of your performance in this matter, don't worry.
DM: I found the fragment! I did find the fragment.
Trok: Where did you find it?
DM: Some secret of the puny humans. Your… some of your companions… he, like, leans over, or doesn't lean over, leans up to look at Trok.
DM: Some of your companions look like humans.
Ryu: Yeah, just… No, no, actually, Ryu will point at Trok, and says in Primordial, “Boss Man.”
DM: How far does the light extend? Maybe if we get… back into the water and swim partway through, we can… We can teleport.

Ryu: Yeah, we leave with the shard, we get it to Rayna, and then we're done.

lines: DM: Collapses into a puddle of water, and you see this, like, vague form in the mist begin to swirl up. And you hear this distant echo in the wind: “Gazankoa will hear of this.”
DM: And then… In the next few minutes, you manage to… kill all these last two creatures, keeping them from swimming off and potentially attacking Rayna.
